source_control.note: This pack closes published learner-study gaps in command signs and warning markings. It uses original explanatory wording and original schematic visuals; it does not copy manual page artwork.

source.locator: NaTIS Road Traffic Signs §3.2 — Minimum speed sign R101/TR101

en.title: Minimum speed sign
en.key_point: Do not drive slower than the speed shown on the sign.
en.explanation: This command sign is used where very slow traffic could disrupt traffic flow. The displayed number is the minimum speed in km/h.

source.locator: NaTIS Road Traffic Signs §3.2 — Keep right R104

en.title: Keep right
en.key_point: Pass to the right of the obstruction when the Keep Right sign applies.
en.explanation: The sign is used at an obstruction such as a traffic island and tells you which side of the obstruction to use.

source.locator: NaTIS Road Traffic Signs §3.2 — Proceed right only R106

en.title: Proceed right only
en.key_point: Drive only in the direction shown by the right-pointing arrow.
en.explanation: This command sign is used at intersections to control the direction in which traffic may proceed.

source.locator: NaTIS Road Traffic Signs §3.2 — Pedestrians only R110

en.title: Pedestrians only
en.key_point: The indicated road or part of the road is reserved for pedestrians.
en.explanation: Drivers and riders must not use the part of the road reserved by this command sign.

source.locator: NaTIS Road Traffic Signs §3.2 — Cyclists only R111

en.title: Cyclists only
en.key_point: The indicated road or part of the road is reserved for cyclists.
en.explanation: Drivers and riders who are not using a pedal cycle must not use the part of the road reserved by this sign.

source.locator: NaTIS Road Traffic Signs §7.2 — Railway crossing ahead WM1

en.title: Railway crossing ahead marking
en.key_point: Slow down and be ready to stop before the railway crossing.
en.explanation: This warning marking is placed before a railway crossing to give additional warning that the crossing is ahead.

source.locator: NaTIS Road Traffic Signs §7.2 — Continuity lines WM2

en.title: Continuity lines
en.key_point: A lane beside a continuity line may soon turn away or meet a break in the roadway.
en.explanation: Check mirrors and blind spots and allow for other traffic changing lanes. The marking warns that an intersection or off-ramp affects the continuing lane arrangement.

source.locator: NaTIS Road Traffic Signs §7.2 — Dividing lines WM3

en.title: Dividing lines
en.key_point: Traffic on the other side of the dividing line is travelling in the opposite direction.
en.explanation: Stay alert for approaching vehicles and keep safely to your side of the road.

source.locator: NaTIS Road Traffic Signs §7.2 — Reversible lane lines WM4

en.title: Reversible lane lines
en.key_point: The direction of traffic in the marked lane can change at different times.
en.explanation: Look for the lane-control signals that apply and be alert for traffic travelling in the opposite direction.

source.locator: NaTIS Road Traffic Signs §3.3 — Height limit R204/TR204

en.title: Height limit
en.key_point: Do not enter if your vehicle or load is higher than the height shown.
en.explanation: The sign warns of a height restriction ahead. Use another route if your vehicle or load exceeds the indicated height.

source.locator: NaTIS Road Traffic Signs §3.3 — Length limit R205/TR205

en.title: Length limit
en.key_point: Do not use the road if your vehicle or combination is longer than the length shown.
en.explanation: The restriction protects roads where long vehicles may not be able to negotiate curves safely.

source.locator: NaTIS Road Traffic Signs §3.3 — Excessive noise prohibited R206

en.title: Excessive noise prohibited
en.key_point: Do not proceed with a vehicle producing excessive noise, and avoid unnecessary hooter use where this sign applies.
en.explanation: The sign is used in noise-sensitive areas. The manual also links it to a restriction on hooter use after the sign.

source.locator: NaTIS Road Traffic Signs §3.3 — Hitch-hiking prohibited R207

en.title: Hitch-hiking prohibited
en.key_point: Do not stop to pick up hitch-hikers where the prohibition applies.
en.explanation: The official learner manual says the sign prohibits hitch-hiking and restricts drivers from picking up passengers for the distance stated in the manual.

source.locator: NaTIS Road Traffic Signs §3.3 — Unauthorised vehicles prohibited R208/TR208

en.title: Unauthorised vehicles prohibited
en.key_point: Do not enter unless you have special authorisation.
en.explanation: This sign closes a road or road section to ordinary traffic. Temporary versions are commonly used at roadworks.

source.locator: NaTIS Road Traffic Signs §3.3 — Left turn ahead prohibited R209/TR209

en.title: Left turn ahead prohibited
en.key_point: Do not turn left at the upcoming intersection.
en.explanation: This prohibition is placed before the junction so you can choose another route before reaching it.

source.locator: NaTIS Road Traffic Signs §3.3 — Right turn ahead prohibited R210/TR210

en.title: Right turn ahead prohibited
en.key_point: Do not turn right at the upcoming intersection.
en.explanation: This prohibition is placed before the junction so you can choose another route before reaching it.

source.locator: NaTIS Road Traffic Signs §3.3 — Overtaking prohibited R214/TR214

en.title: Overtaking prohibited
en.key_point: Do not overtake where the sign applies.
en.explanation: The learner manual associates this sign with a defined prohibition distance. Obey any additional distance or secondary-message information displayed.

source.locator: NaTIS Road Traffic Signs §5.2 — Pre-advance exit direction GA1

en.title: Freeway pre-advance exit direction
en.key_point: An off-ramp exit is coming. If you intend to leave the freeway, prepare to move left in good time.
en.explanation: The manual places this sign well before the exit so drivers have early warning of the routes available ahead.

source.locator: NaTIS Road Traffic Signs §5.2 — Advance exit direction GA2

en.title: Freeway advance exit direction
en.key_point: The freeway exit is getting closer. Move toward the left lane in good time if you are leaving.
en.explanation: This sign gives another advance indication of the exit and destinations served by it.

source.locator: NaTIS Road Traffic Signs §5.2 — Supplementary exit direction GA2/3, TGA2/3

en.title: Supplementary exit direction
en.key_point: If you are taking the exit, you should already be positioning in the extreme left lane.
en.explanation: This sign confirms the approaching off-ramp shortly before the exit.

source.locator: NaTIS Road Traffic Signs §5.2 — Exit direction GA3

en.title: Freeway exit direction
en.key_point: This marks the actual exit. Leave the freeway only from the correct exit lane.
en.explanation: The sign is positioned at or very near the off-ramp to show exactly where the exit begins.

source.locator: NaTIS Road Traffic Signs §5.2 — Gore exit GA4/TGA4

en.title: Gore exit direction
en.key_point: Pass on the exit side if you are leaving the freeway and on the through-road side if you are continuing.
en.explanation: The gore sign marks the separation between the off-ramp and the continuing freeway.

source.locator: NaTIS Road Traffic Signs §5.2 — Advance off-ramp terminal direction GA5

en.title: Advance off-ramp terminal direction
en.key_point: Choose the correct lane before reaching the intersection at the end of the off-ramp.
en.explanation: The sign tells you in advance which lane leads to the destination you want after the off-ramp.

source.locator: NaTIS Road Traffic Signs §5.2 — Off-ramp terminal direction GA6

en.title: Off-ramp terminal direction
en.key_point: Slow down, obey the intersection controls and turn in the direction of your destination.
en.explanation: This sign is placed at the end of the off-ramp and shows the direction of destinations from the intersecting road.
